A solid circular shaft of diameter d = 30 mm and total length L = 1200 mm is fixed (cantilevered) at x = 0 and free at x = 1200 mm.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76 923.1 MPa.
The shaft is loaded by pure torsion only: no transverse shear force, no bending moment, no axial force acts on the shaft.
Two external concentrated torques are applied: T₁ = +200 000 N·mm at x = 1200 mm (free end) and T₂ = −200 000 N·mm at x = 400 mm.
The problem is statically determinate; the reaction torque at the fixed end is found from global equilibrium.
All analysis uses the N–mm–MPa unit system and the small-deformation, linear-elastic assumption.
The polar moment of inertia is J = π d⁴ / 32 and the outer radius is r = d / 2 = 15 mm.
Internal torque in each segment is obtained by the section method: cut the shaft, isolate the free-body to the right of the cut, and enforce ΣM_x = 0 to solve for the internal torque T_int in that segment.
Two segments exist: Segment 1 spans x = 0 to x = 400 mm (length L₁ = 400 mm) and Segment 2 spans x = 400 mm to x = 1200 mm (length L₂ = 800 mm).
Deliverable (a): Report the constant internal torque T_int for Segment 1 and for Segment 2, and present the internal-torque diagram as a piecewise-constant function of x.
Deliverable (b): For each segment, compute the maximum torsional shear stress using τ_max = T_int · r / J, evaluated at the outer fiber. Report τ_max for Segment 1 and Segment 2 separately.
Deliverable (c): Compute the total angle of twist at x = L relative to the fixed base as θ = (T_int,1 · L₁) / (G · J) + (T_int,2 · L₂) / (G · J). Report the result in radians and in degrees.
State explicitly that the reaction torque at x = 0 equals the negative sum of all applied torques, confirming static determinacy.
Do not include any bending, transverse-shear, or axial response in the solution.
